title: Simultaneous normalized integral realization data and comparison predicates
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and use finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and schemes in universe $u$. Define one-field realization data to consist of the normalized coefficient-system evaluation calculus on every scheme, a Roos realization model, and normalized pullback realization models for every scheme map. Require their counit-built system maps to be invertible on intrinsic constructible inputs with $\ell$ invertible, and require the reduction/reconstruction unit to be invertible on constructible inputs. For each embedding $\iota:E\to L$ define scalar realization data by the normalized scalar models with their counit-built maps invertible on constructible inputs. A simultaneous integral comparison system is a family of these one-field data for every finite extension and of scalar data for every embedding, including identities and composites. No existence of such a system is asserted by this definition.
For a supplied system $D$, define the pullback and scalar system counits by applying reduction to the chosen realization and then the actual reduction/total-limit adjunction counit. Define $\eta$ by the realization of the outer pullback followed by total limit of its action on the inner pullback counit. Define the completed compositor by realization, total limit of the whole-system compositor, and $\eta^{-1}$. Define $\lambda$ by scalar realization followed by the scalar action on the pullback counit, and $\mu$ by pullback realization followed by the pullback of the scalar counit and the inverse whole-system scalar/pullback comparison; the scalar comparison is $\lambda\mu^{-1}$. Define the unit from the whole-system identity and the inverse reconstruction unit. Define constructible scalar extension by restriction of the actual completed scalar functor. Its scalar unit is ordinary multiplication conjugated by the specified completion comparison, and its scalar associator is ordinary derived tensor reassociation conjugated by those completion comparisons.
Define the composition-laws predicate by whole-system associativity and both unit equations, together with naturality, associativity and both unit equations for these realized maps. Define the realization-coherence predicate by those composition laws for every field, whole-system and realized scalar/composition equations, naturality of scalar comparison, the rational image of the scalar/composition equation, and the whole-system and realized scalar/scheme-unit, identity-scalar and successive-field associator equations. Scheme equalities use their induced equality transports. These predicates specify equations for the displayed constructions, not new arbitrary comparison maps.
